clue.text: How to break in with a jemmy, showing initiative

parts.note: to break in is to enter a building by force
a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar, used for prising doors open, so working with one is acting prisingly

explanation.surface: A burglary manual explains how to break in with a crowbar, praising the bold approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to' frames the phrase as a method: ENTER (break in) done PRISINGLY (with a jemmy, the burglar's crowbar).
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise is boldness and initiative, so acting with it is acting resourcefully.

clue.text: Theatrical weapon?

parts.note: a stage sword is a fake fencing blade, made of cheap metal rather than steel

explanation.definitionFit: A foil is a fencing sword; a stage one could be made of tin, and the phrase is also kitchen wrapping.

clue.text: Dig up tuber

definitions.meaning: a pig or a searcher rummages in the ground
the underground part of a plant, like a carrot or turnip

explanation.definitionFit: To root is to rummage by digging, as pigs do, and a root vegetable is an underground plant part.

clue.text: Got fat and gave up

definitions.meaning: melted down or clarified fat from meat, as with lard

explanation.definitionFit: Fat is rendered when melted and purified, and a thing rendered is one handed over.

clue.text: Quick look round up-river

indicators.note: the look word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to spy is to look or catch sight of

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the river's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A brief glance around while heading upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DEE into EED, which goes inside SPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy means fast or rapid.

clue.text: As Mimi was by the last act of "La Boheme"

definitions.text: As Mimi was by the last act of "La Boheme"

parts.words: As Mimi was by the last act of "La Boheme"
parts.note: the heroine of Puccini's opera is dying of consumption by its final act, as the opera itself is finishing

explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is close to death in the final act, and the opera too is almost over.

clue.text: Naturally she has her pride

parts.note: a pride is a group of big cats, so a female one naturally belongs to one

explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a family of lions, so the female big cat belongs to one by nature.

clue.text: Mistake at the races? Not if it's a winning one

definitions.text: Mistake at the races? Not if it's a winning one

parts.words: Mistake at the races? Not if it's a winning one
parts.note: a slip at the racecourse sounds like an error, but the punter's paper ticket is welcome when the horse wins

explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's receipt for a wager is called a slip, which also means a mistake.

clue.text: Give out a lightweight sound

indicators.note: the clue's final word tells us to say the phrase aloud and hear another word

parts.note: an ounce is a tiny weight, so a lightweight thing is an ounce

explanation.surface: Someone small makes a faint noise and is told to speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'an ounce' quickly and it sounds like the verb meaning to proclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out news is to declare it publicly.

clue.text: A house celebration in Lincoln

indicators.note: the party word is placed inside the president's short name

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party is held at someone's house in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is the US president, not the English city: ABE holds DO.
explanation.definitionFit: An adobe is a dwelling built of sun-dried clay brick, common in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Blow to a poor player, and quite unfair

definitions.text: Blow to a poor player, and quite unfair

parts.words: Blow to a poor player, and quite unfair
parts.note: a weak player is a rabbit in sporting slang, and a strike to the back of the neck is an illegal hit in boxing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an illegal strike to the back of the neck; a rabbit is also slang for a weak player.

clue.text: Laconic assurance of one in a frenzy

indicators.note: laconic speech is clipped and terse, so the speaker drops the opening pronoun

parts.note: one person reassuring others says 'I am OK'

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped reassurance from somebody who is in fact running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: A laconic speaker trims 'I am OK' to just 'am OK', leaving the reply without its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok means behaving wildly and out of control, in a frenzy.

clue.text: Today a tree may be prepared for a meal

indicators.note: the letters may be arranged into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A fruit tree today might be laid out for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is ready to eat needs no more cooking before it is served.

clue.text: Get-together to name a pear, say

definitions.meaning: a popular British variety of pear is called by this name

explanation.surface: Gathering to choose a name for a new pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A conference is a meeting for discussion, and Conference is a common British pear variety.

clue.text: Makes half-a dozen deliveries, we hear, in Derbyshire

indicators.note: this tells us the phrase is to be heard and spelt as another word

parts.note: in cricket a bowler delivers six balls in an over, so delivering six is bowling an over

explanation.surface: A courier makes six drops in Derbyshire, so we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: The deliveries are cricket balls: six of them make an over. BOLSOVER is a town in Derbyshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolsover is a market town located in the county of Derbyshire, England.

clue.text: Exercise one out of 7 may learn from

indicators.note: exercise the letters, working them around into a new order
the word for one is taken away from the other answer

parts.note: the answer to clue 7-down, the big cat with her pride
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A drill one of seven might pick up something from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal: drop I from the 7-down answer and rearrange the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a piece of teaching that a pupil may take knowledge from.

clue.text: Approach a princess with an amusing character

parts.note: to approach is to come near
Di was the popular name for Diana, Princess of Wales
taken as written, the word an

explanation.surface: Approaching a royal along with a funny companion.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is Diana, Princess of Wales, a regular crossword princess.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a funny performer or someone who is always joking.

clue.text: A right row about the price list

indicators.note: the quarrel word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel or row

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over how much things cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a quarrel (rhymes with 'cow'), not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of charges, such as a hotel's list of room rates.

clue.text: Food obtained by a fiddle in Rhode Island

indicators.note: the stringed instrument goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
a viol is an old bowed stringed instrument, akin to a fiddle

explanation.surface: Dinner obtained through a con in a small New England state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a swindle; here it is the instrument VIOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels with a filling, an Italian dish.

clue.text: Goes down as establishing members

definitions.meaning: a ship that sinks is said to founder
people who set up an organisation are its originators

explanation.definitionFit: To founder is to sink, and the people who found a society are its original establishers.

clue.text: Proper as the laic version

indicators.note: a version of the words is a new form of them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something deemed correct because it matches the layman's account.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct is morally right and proper.

clue.text: Far out, she makes a move again

indicators.note: the letters are put out of place, which signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: A woman a long way off makes another move.
explanation.definitionFit: To start afresh is to begin anew, once more.

clue.text: Fiver due in a way, albeit not vouched for

indicators.note: taking the letters in a way, rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Someone claims a five-pound note is owed to them, though nobody can confirm it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the letters being rearranged; 'a way' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An unverified claim has not been confirmed or attested by anyone.

clue.text: Language we get from Samantha in the East

indicators.note: the letters we get from the run of words sit inside them

explanation.surface: A tongue picked up by someone called Samantha out in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the end of 'Samantha' and the start of 'in'; 'in the East' also hints at Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the official tongue spoken in Thailand.

clue.text: Where capital is lost in this life

indicators.note: the capital, meaning the opening letter, is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: A place where money disappears in this world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' sounds like money but means the first letter: drop W.
explanation.definitionFit: Here in the sense of the present existence, as in 'the here and now'.

clue.text: Cover with honour

definitions.meaning: to top something, as a dentist caps a tooth
to invest a monarch or champion with a title

explanation.definitionFit: To crown is both to cap a tooth or hill and to mark a person with a royal or winning title.

clue.text: Top cardinal virtue?

definitions.meaning: a high point, such as a hill or summit
a Roman Catholic cardinal is addressed by a title of honour, as if his worth were his rank

explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a raised piece of ground, and also the style used for a cardinal, as in 'Your Eminence'.

clue.text: One in a position to tax the wages of sin?

definitions.text: One in a position to tax the wages of sin?

parts.words: One in a position to tax the wages of sin?
parts.note: a finance minister who taxes earnings from wickedness would be the treasury head for wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A government official who could levy duty on the rewards of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: The real title belongs to a university's chief executive; read literally it is the treasury minister of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: The role is the head administrator of a British university, punningly a finance minister for wrongdoing.
